questions.q:
For the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane and anhydrous AlCl3, which statements are correct?
A. Major product is n-propylbenzene.
B. Isopropyl carbocation intermediate is also generated.
C. Multiple substitution is inevitable.
D. Introducing an electron-donating substituent on benzene will not produce any alkylbenzene.
questions.explain: The 1° carbocation rearranges to isopropyl, so the major product is isopropylbenzene. The alkyl product is more reactive, so polysubstitution happens.

questions.q:
The presence of a -NO2 group in a benzene ring:
A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
questions.explain: NO2 withdraws electrons by -M and -I: it deactivates the ring for EAS and makes nucleophilic substitution easier.

questions.q: Benzene on nitration gives nitrobenzene in the presence of HNO3 and H2SO4 mixture, where:
options: both H2SO4 and HNO3 act as bases
HNO3 acts as an acid and H2SO4 as a base
HNO3 acts as a base and H2SO4 as an acid
questions.explain: H2SO4 protonates HNO3, which loses water to form NO2+. The proton acceptor (HNO3) is the base here.

questions.q: The correct sequence of reagents used in the preparation of 4-bromo-2-nitroethylbenzene from benzene is:
questions.explain: Acylate first (no rearrangement), Clemmensen-reduce to ethyl (o/p director), brominate para, then nitration goes ortho to ethyl.

questions.q: Polysubstitution is a major drawback in:
questions.explain: The alkyl product is more reactive than benzene, so it keeps reacting. Acylation products are deactivated, so it stops at one.

questions.q: Which of the following would not give 2-phenylbutane as the major product in a Friedel-Crafts reaction?
questions.explain: Acylation then reduction gives butylbenzene (1-phenylbutane). The others form the secondary butyl cation, giving 2-phenylbutane.

questions.q: Toluene is nitrated and the product is reduced with Sn/HCl. The product is diazotised and then heated with cuprous bromide. The reaction mixture contains:
options: a mixture of o- and p-bromotoluenes
a mixture of o- and p-dibromobenzenes
a mixture of o- and p-bromoanilines
a mixture of o- and m-bromotoluenes
questions.explain: CH3 directs nitration o/p. NO2 → NH2 → N2+ → Br keeps the position, giving o- and p-bromotoluene.

questions.q: Presence of a nitro group in a benzene ring:
options: activates the ring towards electrophilic substitution
deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitution
deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution
questions.explain: NO2 is a strong -M/-I withdrawer, so electrophilic substitution slows down a lot.

questions.q: The reaction of toluene with Cl2 in the presence of FeCl3 gives predominantly:
questions.explain: FeCl3 makes it ring EAS (not side-chain), and CH3 is o/p directing.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of reagents used for converting nitrobenzene into m-dibromobenzene?
questions.explain: NO2 is meta directing, so brominate first. Then reduce to aniline, diazotise, and Sandmeyer swaps N2+ for Br at that same position.
